proof_nl:
Fix an integer n>1 and a real number t with 0<=t<1. Let a=floor(n t). Then a is an integer and, by the defining property of the floor function,
a <= n t < a+1.
Since n>0, dividing by n gives
 a/n <= t < (a+1)/n.
Now fix any k with 1<=k<=n. Because a/n <= t and the floor function is monotone nondecreasing on R, we have
 floor(k a/n) <= floor(k t).
Rearranging,
 -floor(k t)/k <= -floor(k a/n)/k.
Summing this inequality over k=1,2,...,n yields
 - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k <= - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k.
Also, since a=floor(n t), we have floor(n t)=a, and because n(a/n)=a,
 floor(n(a/n))=a.
Therefore
 E_n(t) = floor(n t) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t)/k
       <= a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a/n)/k
       = E_n(a/n).
This is exactly the desired inequality.
solver_summary: Use a=floor(nt), so a/n <= t. Monotonicity of floor gives floor(kt) >= floor(k a/n) for every k, hence the negative sum at t is at most the negative sum at a/n. Since floor(nt)=floor(n(a/n))=a, this yields E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).
vetter_reason: The argument is correct: from a = floor(n t) and a/n <= t, monotonicity of floor gives floor(k a/n) <= floor(k t) for each 1<=k<=n, and summing yields E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n). The endpoint evaluation floor(n(a/n)) = a is valid since n(a/n)=a is an integer. No semantic drift or dependency violation is present.
